text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing a service-edge pod in a Dedicated VPC make authenticated calls to the private-controlplane admin endpoints using a different service account than expected. Quick snapshot of logs below, happened ~14:12 UTC.

sec-bot: automated alert: privilege-escalation-anomaly detected for svcacct:service-edge-runner@redwood-prod. score=0.88

maria: logs (redacted):
```
[2025-06-02T14:12:02Z] POST /admin/v1/tenants/123/actions -> 403
[2025-06-02T14:12:04Z] POST /admin/v1/tenants/123/actions -> 200 (via sa:svc-edge-proxy)
user_agent: service-edge/1.3.0
x-redwood-request-id: r-5df9
```

maria: KMS envelope key used for audit export: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/abcd-ef01

raj: any repro steps? can you dump the service account binding and the exact role grants in that namespace?

maria: repro is flaky but I can reproduce by spinning up a short lived job in the same node pool that curls the metadata endpoint then performs the admin POST. attaching short steps:
```
# run inside node
TOKEN=$(curl -sS http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/identity)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://private-controlplane/admin/v1/tenants/123/actions
```

lucy: looks like the recent RBAC refactor PR (platform/rbac#412) changed the clusterrolebinding selector for svc-edge to include "system:masters" fallback when no ns-scoped role found. I'm pulling the diff now.

sam: audit logs show `impersonation` events originating from a bootstrap controller that runs with node IAM. That controller is supposed to only impersonate backup-svc, but the binding wildcard allowed svc-edge to be matched. gist: https://internal.gist/impersonation-1748

raj: can we quickly block at the network layer? add egress deny for pods in that node pool to private-controlplane IPs until we patch RBAC.

lucy: I can push a short iptables/Calico rule to deny 10.45.2.0/24 -> 10.128.0.0/16 for the node label set. Will do as temporary mitigant.

maria: temp mitigation approved. also we should rotate the service account keys and revoke the offending binding. Who can revoke the clusterrolebinding now?

sam: I can revoke. `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding svc-edge-fallback` then verify audit shows 403 on new attempts.

sec-bot: note: rotate KMS envelope key for audit export after remediation to avoid retained plaintext references. recommend creating new key and re-encrypting any exported logs using key rotation workflow.

raj: followups: 1) remove fallback behavior in rbac refactor and enforce namespace-scoped roles 2) add strict allowlist for admin scopes in webhook admission 3) add explicit impersonation audit metric with alerting 4) add unit test to PR to catch fallback semantics

lucy: I will open rbac/patch PR to remove fallback and add a unit test. tagging reviewers @maria @raj

maria: action items and owners:
- revoke binding now — sam — ETA 15m
- rotate svcacct creds & rotate KMS envelope — raj & maria — ETA 2h
- network deny rule (temp) — lucy — ETA 10m
- patch rbac to remove fallback & tests — lucy — PR by EOD
- add monitoring rule for impersonation anomaly — sam — ETA 4h

sam: done: clusterrolebinding deleted, audit shows new attempts 403. saving deletion command & CID in case we need rollback.

maria: thanks. please paste the final audit export path when you re-encrypt so compliance can ingest. I'll run a postmortem template and tag compliance.

sec-bot: incident-ticket created: INC-2025-1764. severity=P2. linked threads: security, eng-runtime, eng-platform.

maria: keeping this thread for timeline. short postmortem and timeline will go to /docs/incidents/INC-2025-1764. :thumbsup:
